ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  Presentation of Citv Tile to Raneika Brooks for Seven Years of Service to the Citv
  of Malibu

  Mayor Stewart presented the City Tile to Senior Planner Raneika Brooks.

  Senior Planner Raneika Brooks thanked the Council for the recognition.

  Presentation of City Tile to Tyler Eaton for Seven Years of Service to the City of
  Malibu

  Mayor Stewart presented the City Tile to Senior Planner Tyler Eaton.

  Senior Planner Tyler Eaton thanked the Council for the recognition.

ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Acting City Manager Toney provided updates on storm preparations, noting that
  heavy rain is expected Tuesday and Wednesday, with the potential for debris flows.
  He stated the recruitment process for the Community Development Director is now
  open and will close on April 6, 2025. He also discussed Los Angeles County’s
  approval of a $10 million eviction moratorium and rent relief program for
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 10, 2025
  Page 5 of 13

  residential tenants affected by the fires, with protections in place until July 31,
  2025. However, the ordinance does not extend to small businesses. The Council
  expressed interest in following up on potential relief options for commercial
  tenants.

  Acting City Manager Toney reported the Rebuild Center opened successfully,
  hosting over 20 appointments on its first day. He stated an open house is scheduled
  for March 19 from 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. He also explained that weekly neighborhood-
  speciflc meetings are set to launch soon, with details to be posted on
  MalibuRebuilds.org. The Council expressed interest in data tracking on rebuilding
  applications, including the type of rebuilds, neighborhood distribution, and the
  number of properties listed for sale.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, Acting City Manager Toney stated staffwill
  collect data on rebuilding applications and provide periodic updates.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, provided the
  monthly crimes report for February 2025. He reported a 40.8% year-over-year
  decrease in reported Part 1 crimes for February, with 42 incidents recorded. He
  discussed significant incidents during the month, including a 2023 burglary case
  was solved through DNA evidence. Additionally, a mountain lion was struck and
  killed on Kanan Dume Road, prompting a reminder for drivers to slow down in
  wildlife areas. He emphasized the importance of emergency preparedness due to
  the earthquakes in Decker Canyon. He discussed the deadlines for wildfire recovery
  programs, including Los Angeles County household relief grants, small business
  relief funds, and worker relief funds, and FEMA financial assistance and small
  business disaster loans. He explained the Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) access pass
  distribution is now available three days a week at designated locations.

  In response to Councilmember Conrad, Sergeant Soderlund stated the PCH closure
  checkpoint must remain in place for visibility and enforcement purposes.

RECESS  At 6:23 p.m., Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 6:34
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion to
  hear Item No. 7A. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Luca Iacovoni discussed the recent City Council Workshop regarding the fire
  rebuild ordinance. He expressed concern that the workshop was not comprehensive
  enough to facilitate an easier rebuild process for affected residents.

  Dean Wenner addressed the Council regarding the number of homes that remain to
  be rebuilt following multiple fires in Malibu. He proposed the creation of a Rebuild
  Czar position and expressed his interest in serving in that role.

  Christopher Sorensen shared solutions proposed by the Malibu Architects
  Association aimed at increasing efficiency in the fire rebuild process. He suggested
  the implementation of sewer lines, prefabricated construction, and fire-smart
  design, stating these could result in cost savings for residents.

  Michel Shane discussed the upcoming parole hearing for the individual responsible
  for the death of Emily Shane.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 10, 2025
  Page 7 of 13

Kristin Thames expressed concern for vulnerable individuals, particularly seniors,
during wildfires. She proposed the formation of a task force to develop solutions to
better assist seniors during emergency situations.

Luis Tena commented on the recent City Council Workshop for the fire rebuild
ordinance, expressing concern over the interpretation of FEMA elevation
requirements and the potential for de minimis waivers to be appealed to the
California Coastal Commission. He requested that the City invest in development
services software to streamline the rebuild process.

Jo Drummond thanked Principal Planners Brooks and Eaton for their years of
service. She expressed concern over new irrigation requirements and the removal
of the bulk standard from the proposed rebuild ordinance. She proposed reducing
the number ofrequired inspections for rebuilds and supported the idea of appointing
a Rebuild Czar. She also advocated for the use of goats in fuel modification efforts.

Norm Haynie thanked and commended Environmental Sustainability Director
Bundy and Principal Planners Brooks and Eaton for their work during the Franklin
and Palisades Fires. He encouraged residents to maintain on-site water supplies
such as water tanks for fire protection.

Abe Roy discussed the creation of a resident developed fire rebuild website.

Arno Koch discussed delays affecting the rebuild process and advocated for the use
of measurable statistics to increase transparency. He also supported expediting the
review of self-containment features such as pools.

Kevin Keegan raised concerns about ocean water safety in the aftermath of the
Palisades Fire and requested a presentation on the topic at a future Council meeting.
He advocated for the use of a mobile app instead of paper passes for PCH access
and inquired about the City's use of artificial intelligence (AI) to improve the
rebuild process. He also asked for Council support for a request to the Santa
Monica-Malibu Unified School District (SM-MUSD) for school resource officers
in local schools.

Scott Dittrich spoke about the ongoing undergrounding of electrical lines. He noted
that telecom companies were still using existing poles. He requested that the City
facilitate communication between the utilities to coordinate efforts. He commended
the City-hosted workshop and requested more on fire-related topics.

Chris Goldblatt introduced the Fish Reef Project, an initiative aimed at converting
barren seafloor areas into new marine ecosystems. He shared the organization’s
mission with the Council.

Jefferson Wagner expressed concern over inconsistent issuance of PCH passes and
stated that programs like Meals on Wheels have experienced difficulty accessing
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 10, 2025
  Page 8 of 13

  neighborhoods. He noted that developer Scott Gillen is obligated to contribute
  $72,000 to the City's skatepark and expressed interest in the Rebuild Czar position.
  He also proposed rezoning vacant commercial properties along PCH for residential
  or mixed-use development.

  Kraig Hill discussed delays caused by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and Phase
  II debris removal. He noted that, despite the City’s plastic bag ban, plastic sandbags
  are being used. He also expressed concern that planning job postings were not listed
  on the City’s website. He discussed recent grading of the vacant lot near Winter
  Canyon Road.

  Pamela Conley Ulich requested a moment of silence in memory of Betty O’Meara,
  who passed away during the Palisades Fire. She proposed a “Betty Buddy” program
  to assist seniors during emergencies and emphasized the need to appoint an Interim
  City Manager.

  Kimberly Carr presented mobility solutions for the PCH closure, including
  expanded Metro bus service, water taxis, vanpool programs, and park-and—ride
  initiatives.

  Howard Rudski thanked Principal Planners Brooks and Eaton and Environmental
  Sustainability Director Bundy. He expressed support for Michel Shane’s
  comments. He recommended working with lobbyists and officials in the
  Governor’s Office rather than sending letters on rebuild issues.

  Wade Major stated concerns over telecom companies not collaborating with SCE
  to underground all utilities.

  Andy Lyon stated that PCH should remain open to all Malibu residents but stopping
  should be prohibited, with neighborhood access limited. He also raised concerns
  regarding grading on a lot near Winter Canyon Road.

  Ryan Embree recommended that the City enter into a funding agreement with
  FEMA to ensure reimbursement for fire—related expenditures. He proposed that the
  City hire a utility undergrounding expert to coordinate infrastructure improvements
  and a grant writer to pursue all available funding opportunities. He indicated
  support for the implementation of speed cameras and the use of electronic
  transponders for resident access to PCH

ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Conrad expressed concern that houses in the City were being used
  as short-term rentals after so many residents were displaced by the fires. She
  advocated for the City to reconsider a ban on short-term rentals so the properties
  can be used for long-term occupancy. She suggested that, given the current housing
  crisis, the California Coastal Commission may now support such a policy change
  and requested that the Council revisit the matter. She also requested Council
   Malibu City COuncil
  Minutes of March 10, 2025
  Page 9 of 13

support for the formation of a senior task force. She asked for additional
information on the process to convert a commercial property for residential use.
She also inquired about obtaining a photograph of a criminal suspect to help raise
community awareness.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Acting City Manager Toney indicated they
would contact the Sheriff‘s Department to determine if the image could be released
for public dissemination.

Councilmember Conrad inquired about the City's role in utility undergrounding
efforts and indicated support for the City advocating for undergrounding all
utilities.

In response to Councilmember Conrad, Acting City Manager Toney responded that
CALFIRE had graded the site at the corner of Malibu Canyon and PCH under
emergency provisions and noted that the lot had been previously graded for nursery
use. He explained that site remediation is required to be completed within nine
months.

Councilmember Uhring expressed support for efforts to underground utility lines
throughout the City and stated that he was uncertain about the appropriate process
for communicating with the Califomia Public Utilities Commission. He suggested
the City consider submitting a formal letter to take a position and advocate for full
utility undergrounding. He discussed concerns about uninhabited and damaged
beachfront properties, noting the environmental and public health hazards posed by
the debris and deteriorating structures. He expressed frustration that several
property owners had not submitted Right of Entry forms and stated that efforts by
Environmental Sustainability Director Bundy to make contact have been met with
silence in many cases. He questioned whether any existing laws would allow the
City—or agencies such as the Army Corps of Engineers to intervene without
property owner consent.
Interim City Attorney Rusin responded that in order for the City to act unilaterally,
a strong legal showing would be required, such as proving the existence of a public
nuisance. Additionally, the City would be responsible for the cost ofremoval unless
a funding source were identified. He noted that the Army Corps of Engineers has
broader authority than the City and could potentially undertake such work, but
action would likely require support from the Governor’s Office.

Deputy City Manager Brown clarified that the City had previously submitted a
letter to the Governor, approved at the Special City Council meeting on February
27, requesting that beachfront home cleanups particularly related to septic
systems be included in Phase II of debris removal. She explained that for the
Army Corps of Engineers to take action, the Govemor must first direct CalOES
(California Office of Emergency Services) to include these efforts as part of the
state emergency. She stated staff is actively engaged in seeking resolution and
advocating for accelerated cleanup efforts.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 10, 2025
  Page 10 of 13

Councilmember Silverstein stated regarding the hazards on Malibu beaches, that
the City has the authority to declare a local emergency in situations where the
health, safety, and welfare of the community are at risk. He referenced prior
precedent in which a local emergency was declared related to PCH and suggested
that the City exercise similar authority in this instance. He stated that such a
declaration could provide expanded powers and legal immunity for emergency
actions taken in good faith, He indicated support for bringing a timely item with
clear options for legal action against the beach hazards,

In response to Councilmember Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin confirmed
he could prepare such a report and bring it to a future meeting.

Councilmember Silverstein discussed the importance of supporting local
businesses and flre Victims. He stated he Visited the Community Closet donation
center; he praised this initiative for simultaneously supporting both businesses and
fire victims and encouraged community members to participate. He discussed the
challenges to rebuilding, including the limited capacity of City staff. He discussed
the importance of reducing bureaucratic barriers and suggested follow the models
of the City of Los Angeles and County of Los Angeles, including self-certification
and resource scaling. He proposed the establishment of an independent, resident-
led rebuild management team or liaison. He requested the item be agendized for
discussion at an upcoming meeting. He addressed confusion surrounding Coastal
Commission jurisdiction over flre rebuilds under the Governor’s executive order.
He encouraged residents to rebuild like-for-like to retain the benefits available to
them under the Governor’s executive order and avoid the complexity and
uncertainty of CDP review. He expressed that non-like-for—like applicants should
not be eligible for use ofthe Rebuild Center. He asked Acting City Manager Toney
to investigate claims that employees of Nobu and Soho House were receiving PCH
access passes. He stated that, unless all Malibu workers are deemed essential, those
employees should not qualify for such passes and any improperly issued passes
should be revoked. He thanked Kraig Hill for his service on the Planning
Commission. He announced his intent to appoint a new Planning Commissioner
with no professional development background, for a fresh perspective. He
expressed concerns about grading on the lot at the comer of PCH and Malibu
Canyon Road. He urged the City to ensure that similar damage is prevented at the
site.

Mayor Pro Tem Riggins commended Acting City Manager Toney and Deputy City
Manager Brown for their exceptional leadership during the ongoing recovery
period. She stated that both have diligently staffed numerous meetings, ensured the
Emergency Operations Center (EOC) functions were maintained, and kept general
City operations running. She emphasized that PCH will continue to be impacted
with infrastructure challenges such as debris removal, undergrounding, and
reconstruction. She acknowledged the hardship this poses for commuters and urged
residents to utilize the Metro bus. She stressed the importance of submitting Right
of Entry (ROE) forms for debris removal, noting that those opting in or out must
submit their paperwork. She urged residents to comply promptly to facilitate
cleanup efforts. She reminded seniors to contact the Senior Center with any special
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 10, 2025
  Page 11 of 13

requests 0r questions. She encouraged the resumption of programs like Meals on
Wheels and praised the City’s efforts to restart Dial-A-Ride. She stated that the
Malibu Rebuild Center had officially opened, with an open house scheduled for
March 19 from 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. She encouraged residents to Visit the center, where
staff are available by appointment to provide guidance on rebuild requirements,
application timelines, and building plan submittals. She pointed residents to the
MalibuRebuilds.org website for additional resources. She confirmed that a
Southern California Edison (SCE) town hall meeting is scheduled for Thursday,
March 20, 2025, and supported the idea of inviting telecommunications companies
to participate. She asked for Council consensus to bring back a future agenda item
to discuss potential City funding for a school resource officer, including discussion
of cost-sharing responsibilities with the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School
District.

In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Acting City Manager Toney responded that
the City has been documenting all disaster—related expenses and submitting
reimbursement requests to FEMA, noting the City has complied with all procedural
requirements.

Mayor Stewart stated the current event qualifies for 100 percent FEMA
reimbursement for the first six months of eligible expenses under Categories A and
B. Mayor Stewart stated he appreciated Commissioner Hill’s service to the City.
He wished him the best in rebuilding his home and expressed hope that the City
would be able to provide meaningful support during the process. He offered high
praise for Acting City Manager Toney and Deputy City Manager Brown. He
commended their leadership and stated that he was proud to work alongside them.
He shared a positive experience from a recent visit to the Malibu Rebuild Center.
He reported that the City had submitted a letter to federal officials, at the request of
the Governor’s Office, in support of securing $39.6 million in disaster funding. The
letter was submitted in coordination with the City of Los Angeles and Malibu. He
also stated the City has a professional grant writing service under contract, with
specialists dedicated to specific grant categories. He explained that individuals
employed within Malibu, regardless of occupation, are eligible for essential worker
passes to access PCH. He emphasized that many workers in the restaurant and
service industries rely on Malibu jobs for their livelihood, and the City is making
efforts to preserve their employment by ensuring access and business continuity.
He addressed concerns regarding water supply requirements for fire rebuilds. He
stated that EPA staging sites at Topanga and Will Rogers Beach have been
dismantled and decommissioned. He stated the remaining debris and household
waste from opt—out properties are being processed through Phase l contractors or
the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and transported to designated facilities,
including a recycling site at Temescal and a final disposal location in Nevada. He
encouraged use of the Metro bus line. He noted that TAP cards can be purchased
and reloaded at the Malibu Library and recommended the metro app to track bus
locations in real time. He emphasized that this is a reliable transportation alternative
during prolonged PCH impacts. He also highlighted the availability of the City's
Dial-A-Ride service, which offers transportation for seniors and individuals with
medical needs to destinations in Santa Monica, West Los Angeles, and the San
   Malibu City Council

  Fernando Valley. He stated that Southern California Edison (SCE) is required by
  the Public Utilities Commission (PUC) to underground major electrical circuits,
  including those that serve Malibu. He stated SCE is proceeding with
  undergrounding efforts from the east side of the City westward, particularly in fire-
  impacted areas, with the goal of expediting completion timelines. He stated that
  although SCE and telecommunications companies are not legally required to share
  trenching operations, current plans along PCH involve coordinated undergrounding
  in a single trench.

RECESS  At 9:07 p.m., Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 9:16
